definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK: from the landed candidate-pack tree, prove whether the exact WindowsPackToolchain manifest and sanitized child PATH still omit Cargo; if another row already landed an equivalent authenticated Cargo carrier, adopt and verify it rather than duplicating it.

The frozen pack-tool/toolchain-pin schemas carry one Cargo PackToolLaunch resolved from the pinned Rust 1.96.0 toolchain, with exact executable identity and version/digest pins; missing, extra, malformed, wrong-version, wrong-digest, in-repository, symlinked, or changed Cargo refuses at the packaging toolchain layer with the existing stable PACK_STEP_FAILED code.

Serialization and parsing preserve exact key sets and immutable argv/identity witnesses; packWindowsFromCommit leases the Cargo executable and adds only its canonical external directory to the sanitized child PATH, with no ambient PATH, USERPROFILE, CARGO_HOME, shell, or command-string authority.

Focused tests assert both manifest directions and prove the materialized child can launch only the carried Cargo identity; substituting a same-name executable or mutating the Cargo digest reds the named refusal assertion.
The seven owned paths remain within production-file caps, focused packaging tests execute with nonzero Test Files/Tests counts, and pnpm typecheck:packaging exits 0.

TWO FIXTURE REDS WERE FOR THE WRONG REASON AND WERE FIXED BEFORE BANKING THE RED, per "a red for the wrong reason is not a red-first":
- First run gave `Error: PACK_STEP_FAILED: pnpm version mismatch` on three arms. Cause: I had injected `powershellExecutable: process.execPath`, so `execute()` used NODE as the leased-process broker when running `pnpm --version`. Dropped that override so the real protected PowerShell brokers the call (production's own path). The pnpm leg now resolves green and the arms reach the Cargo leg. This also means the positive arm is the FIRST test in the repo to drive `resolveWindowsPackToolchain` all the way to a successful resolve — the pre-existing arm at :536 only ever asserted a throw at the node fence.
- The symlink case gave `Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink ...`; file symlinks need privilege on this host. Replaced with a DIRECTORY junction over the pinned `bin` directory, so the executable path still traverses a link and `canonicalPath()` still refuses, with no privilege requirement.

A REAL PINNED CARGO EXISTS ON THIS HOST, so the positive arms are genuine and not mock-backed: `C:\Users\Yaron\.rustup\toolchains\1.96.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\bin\cargo.exe`, sha256 `122f18d28a63fa358f3db266abee1ff1d8aabf0ab7f2dd9ac38a38da99977ae5` — byte-identical to `cargoSha256` in cargo-toolchain-pins.json. DIVERGENCE (epic rail 7A) — stated explicitly, since this is what makes arms 4 and 5 non-vacuous: every sibling fence inside `resolveWindowsPackToolchain` throws a PLAIN `Error` whose message carries a `": <detail>"` suffix (`node provenance invalid`, `PowerShell unavailable`, `pnpm provenance invalid`, `pnpm version mismatch`). The Cargo guard is the ONLY mechanism that can produce a `PackCargoToolError`, a distinct class carrying `code: PACK_STEP_FAILED` AND `layer: PACKAGING_TOOLCHAIN` AND the bare message `"PACK_STEP_FAILED"`. `cargoRefusal()` asserts instance, code, layer and exact message together, so a sibling fence answering first cannot keep these arms green — it produces a different class and a suffixed message. That is the "seam PRODUCES distinguishable results" form of divergence; no redundant call was deleted. Proven live: the first run's `pnpm version mismatch` red surfaced as `expected Error: PACK_STEP_FAILED: pnpm version mis… to be an instance of PackCargoToolError` — the helper correctly refused to accept a foreign fence as a pass.

(a) pack-command.ts — Cargo wired through the EXISTING authority, no admission inlined:
- `const CARGO_PINS = readCargoToolchainPins();` added beside the existing `const PINS = readToolchainPins();`, mirroring that idiom. `resolveCargoPackTool` now passes `CARGO_PINS` instead of calling `readCargoToolchainPins()` per invocation, so THE PIN FILE IS READ ONCE PER MODULE LOAD, not twice. `resolveCargoPackTool` keeps arity 2, so the landed `expect(resolveCargoPackTool).toHaveLength(2)` assertion in pack-cargo-tool.test.ts still holds (verified green).
- `ToolResolutionDependencies` gains `readonly cargoExecutable?: string;` — the same explicit-executable seam `powershellExecutable` already uses.
- New private `pinnedCargoExecutable(environment)`: reads `RUSTUP_HOME`, else `USERPROFILE` + ".rustup", from the PASSED environment (the pnpm leg's own idiom), and returns `<rustup>/toolchains/<CARGO_PINS.toolchain>/bin/cargo.exe`. NEVER an ambient PATH lookup, never a repository path; the toolchain segment comes from the pin, not a hard-coded literal, so no second Cargo vocabulary exists. When neither variable yields an absolute root it throws the ALREADY-LANDED `PackCargoToolError` — the same class, same `PACK_STEP_FAILED` code, same `PACKAGING_TOOLCHAIN` layer. Zero new refusal vocabulary was introduced.
- `resolveWindowsPackToolchain` resolves `cargo` via `resolveCargoPackTool(repositoryRoot, dependencies.cargoExecutable ?? pinnedCargoExecutable(environment))` and returns it in the frozen manifest. `pack-cargo-tool.ts` remains the sole Cargo authority.
